Khādira Gṛhyasūtras
------------------------------------------
The गृह्यसूत्रस् and the धर्म-sūtras—which themselves form a part of the कल्पसूत्रस्, the last of the six Vedāṅgas—are the forerunners of the dharmaśāstra literature.
The Khādira Gṛhyasūtras belonging to the tradition of the Rāṇāyanīya school of the Sāmaveda seems to be an abridgement of and an improvement over the earlier work Gobhila Gṛhyasūtras. It has 580 sūtras distributed over 19 khaṇḍas or sections, which themselves have been accommodated in 4 paṭalas or chapters.
The first paṭala deals with समावर्तन (returning from the होउसे of the गुरु after एदुचतिओन्) and with विवाह or the मर्रिअगे ceremonies in great detail.
The second paṭala describes the following ceremonies: Darśa and Pūrṇamāsa sacrifices; the पुṁसवन and the सीमन्तोन्नयन ceremonies for a pregnant woman; (See under the respective titles for more details.); नामकरण or the naming ceremony of the child; चौल or tonsure of the hair in the third year; उपनयन sacrament; गोदान or first shaving of the beard; some vratas or religious vows like the Godānavrata, the आदित्यव्रत and the Upaniṣadvrata.
The third paṭala deals with the ceremonies connected with the student who has completed his studies and is becoming a स्नातक, the आग्रयण rite, the Anvaṣṭakya rite and the Piṇḍapitṛ-यज्ञ.
The fourth—the last—paṭala gives instructions regarding the various kāmya (desire-motivated) rites to be performed by those desiring brahmavarcas (lustre of ब्रह्मन्), cattle, wealth, property, averting untimely or accidental death, getting rid of misfortune, instructions regarding building one’s होउसे, attaining long life, undisturbed means of livelihood, cure from the bites of poisonous animals and honouring respectable persons like one’s teacher with मधुपर्क.
